articles.title: Joey Barton to remain in custody until trial after bail application turned down
articles.summary: Former footballer accused of attack outside golf club. His trial has been pushed back to March next year. The former footballer Joey Barton will remain in custody until his trial next year after a bail application was refused.
body: The 44-year-old had been due to stand trial at Liverpool crown court last week accused of causing grievous bodily harm with intent to Kevin Lynch, 51, at Fairway, Huyton, on 8 March. But on Wednesday the case was adjourned and put back to March next year.

Barton, wearing a grey zip-up fleece, appeared over video link from HMP Liverpool at a hearing on Monday, when Judge David Potter refused a renewed bail application. Barton nodded as the judge remanded him in custody in advance of a pre-trial hearing on 11 December.
His trial will take place exactly a year after the alleged assault, meaning the defendant, who was arrested shortly after the incident, will have spent 12 months on remand.

Barton is accused of carrying out the attack on Lynch after they had been drinking together at Huyton and Prescot golf club. Lynch, a former non-league football manager and founder of the special education school NexGen Academy, was said to have sustained serious injuries to an eye.

articles.title: Chelsea explored move for Fulham midfielder Berge
articles.summary: Chelsea showed late interest in Fulham's Sander Berge as they attempted to strengthen their midfield options before Enzo Fernandez's departure.
body: The Blues intended to sign a central midfielder in the closing days of the summer transfer window as they prepared for Fernandez to join Manchester City.
However, Chelsea 's search ended in disappointment as they sold Fernandez for £125m without signing a replacement.

It is understood Norway international Berge was among the options explored by Chelsea during the final stages of the window, though they did not make a formal bid and Fulham considered the 28-year-old not for sale.
Since his arrival from Burnley in 2023, Berge has become a key player for the Cottagers, making 78 appearances.

articles.title: Chelsea’s midfield a headache for Alonso after Arsenal press advantage | Jacob Steinberg
articles.summary: There was a gulf between the teams in the middle of the park, with Moisés Caicedo’s absence hurting the visitors. There have been seasons when Chelsea have turned up at the Emirates Stadium and parked the bus.
body: The plan worked at times. Chelsea maintained their habit of scoring early goals, going ahead through Morgan Rogers, and created further openings. But they were facing the champions and do not have Arsenal’s completeness. Shortcomings were exploited, particularly in midfield. Declan Rice romped through the middle at one point and the winning goal owed much to Reece James losing track of Martin Ødegaard as Arsenal’s captain strode through to fire past Emiliano Martínez.

There is much to like about Alonso’s vision. Chelsea are not obsessed with possession and are speeding forward on the counterattack. Yet while they look menacing with every attack there is a cost to the chaos. Alonso has found balance elusive. Chelsea have conceded seven goals in three games, are without a clean sheet in the league since January and need the oomph provided by Caicedo if they are to make this full-throttle style work.

articles.title: Pakistan launch player conduct investigation during dysfunctional England tour
articles.summary: Mobile phones of players confiscated as part of inquiry. Nine fined during Pakistan’s recent tour of Caribbean. Pakistan have launched an investigation into “discipline and conduct” during their highly dysfunctional tour of England, with two players understood to have had their mobile phones…
body: A spokesperson for the Pakistan Cricket Board confirmed on Monday that an investigation is currently under way and while no individuals have been named, it follows the removal of seven players from their original touring party last week in response to going 2-0 down with one Test still to play.

The Guardian understands that, as part of this, two players had data from their mobile phones captured by PCB security officials. This is said to have occurred during the aftermath of the team’s 194-run defeat in the second Test at Lord’s.

Amir Mir, the PCB head of communications, wrote on X: “The Pakistan Cricket Board has initiated an internal disciplinary inquiry following media reports concerning discipline and conduct, which are currently being reviewed internally.
“The PCB handles such matters in accordance with its standard procedures. The process is being conducted under PCB regulations, ensuring that all concerned individuals are given due consideration.”

articles.title: Can Kane buck history and win Ballon d'Or?
articles.summary: History suggests Ballon d’Or winners come from those who have recently lifted one of football's biggest trophies. Can Harry Kane become a rare exception?
body: With the Ballon d'Or shortlist to be announced on Tuesday, Harry Kane heads the field as the bookmakers' favourite after a prolific season for club and country. History, however, suggests football's biggest individual prize is rarely decided on goals alone.
Since the Ballon d'Or was first awarded in 1956, performances in the game's biggest competitions have consistently shaped the outcome.

World Cup years, in particular, have followed a remarkably clear pattern and recent editions have shown just how difficult it is to win the award without lifting a major global or continental tournament.
Once the nominees are announced, an international jury of specialised journalists will cast their votes, with one representative per country from the men's top 100 having their say.

articles.title: Williams and Sheehan join Bellamy's Wales staff
articles.summary: Ex-Wales captain Ashley Williams and former Swansea boss Alan Sheehan join Craig Bellamy's backroom staff before Wales' Nations League campaign.
body: Former Wales captain Ashley Williams and ex-Swansea boss Alan Sheehan have joined Craig Bellamy's backroom staff as assistant coaches before Wales' Nations League campaign.
Williams, 42, played 86 times for Wales and skippered the side during their memorable run to the Euro 2016 semi-final.
The former central defender, a Uefa A Licence holder, has recently been involved in coaching at several Wales age group camps but this is his first senior role.
Sheehan, 39, was sacked as head coach of Swansea in November 2025, the former Republic of Ireland youth international having previously been an assistant coach at Swansea, Southampton and Luton Town.

articles.title: Pietersen joins England's white-ball coaching team
articles.summary: England appoint former Ashes-winning batter Kevin Pietersen to their white-ball coaching team in the build-up to the 2027 ICC Cricket World Cup.
body: Pietersen, 46, joins as a specialist mentor and will start in the role for the upcoming T20 and one-day matches against Sri Lanka.

He will also be involved in this winter's tours to Australia and South Africa, before joining up with the teams again for the home series against Pakistan and New Zealand next summer, as well as the 50-over World Cup, which is being held in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia in the autumn.
"I've got immense respect for KP and what he's achieved in the game," said England's white-ball head coach Brendon McCullum.
"He's had an amazing impact on English cricket, so for someone with his experience, knowledge and stature to want to play a role with this team is a fantastic result."

articles.summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board has launched an investigation into "media reports concerning discipline and conduct" amid the team's crisis tour of England.
body: Pakistan last week took the unprecedented step of sending seven players home and calling up seven after losing heavily at Headingley and Lord's to fall 2-0 down in the three-match series.

Head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and assistant Umar Gul have also been replaced, with Mike Hesson, in charge of Pakistan's white-ball sides, and former Australia seamer Ashley Noffke overseeing the third Test at Edgbaston, which begins on Wednesday.
A statement read: "The Pakistan Cricket Board has initiated an internal disciplinary inquiry following media reports concerning discipline and conduct, which are currently being reviewed internally.

articles.title: Mourinho gets a sprinkler—and a reminder of his famous Camp Nou celebration
articles.summary: After his pre-match press conference at Valdebebas ahead of Real Madrid’s Champions League opener against Inter Milan, José Mourinho was approached by Italian journalist Tancredi Palmeri, who handed him a garden sprinkler.
body: The gift was a nod to the second leg of the 2010 Champions League semi-final at Camp Nou. Having won the first leg 3–1, Mourinho’s Inter lost 1–0 that night but advanced 3–2 on aggregate, eliminating Pep Guardiola’s Barcelona. At the final whistle, Mourinho raced onto the pitch to celebrate with his players. Camp Nou staff turned on the sprinklers in an attempt to cut the celebrations short, creating one of the most iconic images of his career: Mourinho celebrating as water sprayed around him.

Despite his fond memories with Inter, Mourinho is fully focused on Real Madrid. Inter is now led by his former player Cristian Chivu. The Real Madrid boss said he loves Chivu, but greetings are reserved for before and after the game only. During the game, Mourinho is locked in for Real Madrid only.

articles.title: Farrell on retirement, fond memories, and next steps with Wigan
articles.summary: Wigan Warriors captain Liam Farrell says he is not sure if he will play for the club again after he announced he will retireat the end of the 2026 Super League season.
body: The 36-year-old, who has only ever played for the Warriors, will call time on a career which has spanned 17 professional seasons. Farrell has captained Wigan since 2023 and been capped 12 times by England.
He has totalled 428 appearances for Wigan and scored 151 tries, winning six Super League titles, five Challenge Cups and two World Club Challenge successes during his illustrious career.

Farrell has not featured since June with an ongoing neck issue and with just three potential matches remaining in the season for his club, the chances of him featuring again for his boyhood club are in doubt.
That third match, if Wigan were to make it, would be the Super League Grand Final at Old Trafford on October 3, live on Sky Sports.

The famous question posed by meteorologist Edward Lorenz back in the 1970s was 'can the flap of a butterfly's wing in Brazil set off a tornado in Texas?'
